skill.name: auth-implementation-patterns
skill.description: Master authentication and authorization patterns for JWT, OAuth2, sessions, RBAC, password security, and API access control.
skill.summary: Provides secure authentication and authorization implementation patterns for TypeScript and Express applications.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: The static shell, environment, sensitive file, and reconnaissance findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences and non-executed TypeScript examples. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found. One content-level issue remains: the OAuth example places an access token in a URL query string.

remediation.issue: OAuth callback example exposes an access token in the URL.
remediation.suggestion: Change the example to use an authorization code exchange or set tokens in secure, httpOnly, sameSite cookies after server-side validation.

semantic_findings.title: Access Token Exposed in OAuth Callback URL
semantic_findings.description: The OAuth example redirects the access token in the URL query string. Access tokens in URLs can leak through browser history, server logs, analytics, and referrer headers.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 345 explicitly appends tokens.accessToken to the callback URL. This is a recognized OAuth implementation risk, although it appears to be insecure guidance rather than malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Authentication code often fails through weak token, session, or role checks. This skill gives practical patterns for secure access control design.
actual_capabilities: Explains JWT access tokens, refresh tokens, verification, and Express authentication middleware.
Shows refresh token storage, expiration checks, revocation, and logout flows.
Covers session-based authentication with Redis-backed Express sessions and secure cookie flags.
Demonstrates OAuth2 social login with Passport.js providers and callback handling.
Provides RBAC, permission checks, and resource ownership authorization patterns.
Includes password hashing, password validation, and rate limiting examples for auth endpoints.
limitations: Examples focus on TypeScript, Express, Passport.js, Redis, and common Node.js libraries.
The skill is guidance, not a complete production authentication framework.
Database calls are illustrative and must be adapted to the user project schema.
It does not replace threat modeling, penetration testing, or compliance review.

use_cases.title: Add JWT Authentication
use_cases.description: Implement access tokens, refresh tokens, verification middleware, and logout behavior for an API.

use_cases.title: Design Authorization Rules
use_cases.description: Map roles, permissions, and resource ownership checks before exposing protected endpoints.

use_cases.title: Review Auth Security
use_cases.description: Compare an existing authentication flow against recommended token, session, cookie, and rate limit controls.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Auth Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a new app authentication flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between session authentication, JWT, and OAuth2 for my application. Ask about my stack, clients, deployment model, and security needs.

prompt_templates.title: Implement JWT Login
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer adding token-based authentication to an Express API.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a JWT login flow with short-lived access tokens, hashed refresh tokens, token revocation, and Express middleware.

prompt_templates.title: Add RBAC and Ownership Checks
prompt_templates.scenario: Team extending an API with protected admin and user-owned resources.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to define roles, permissions, middleware, and ownership checks for these routes. Include denial cases and tests to cover authorization failures.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Existing Auth Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a production authentication design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my authentication and authorization design against this skill. Identify token, session, OAuth2, password, rate limiting, and RBAC risks with prioritized fixes.

output_examples.input: I need secure login for an Express API used by a web app and mobile app.
output_examples.output: A recommended JWT and refresh token design, including token lifetimes, storage guidance, revocation behavior, and middleware responsibilities.

output_examples.input: I need admins, moderators, and regular users to access different endpoints.
output_examples.output: A role and permission plan that separates authentication from authorization and adds server-side checks for each protected route.

output_examples.input: I want to review my session cookie configuration before launch.
output_examples.output: A checklist for httpOnly, secure, sameSite, expiration, Redis session storage, CSRF protection, and logout behavior.

best_practices: Use short-lived access tokens and store refresh tokens with hashing and revocation support.
Enforce authorization on the server for every protected route and resource operation.
Protect authentication endpoints with rate limits, strong password hashing, and secure cookies when sessions are used.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on client-side role checks as the only authorization control.
Do not store passwords, refresh tokens, or session secrets in plaintext.
Do not place long-lived access tokens in browser-visible URLs or unsafe storage.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a complete auth service?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples that must be adapted to your application, database, and threat model.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it cover both authentication and authorization?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers identity verification, tokens, sessions, OAuth2, roles, permissions, and resource ownership checks.

faq.question: Is it limited to Node.js applications?
faq.answer: The examples use TypeScript and Express, but the architectural patterns can guide other backend stacks.

faq.question: Does it include password security guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes password validation, bcrypt hashing, login rate limiting, and common password handling pitfalls.

faq.question: Should I still run a security review?
faq.answer: Yes. Use this skill as implementation guidance, then perform threat modeling, testing, and compliance review for production systems.
